Both components take a View (V) as input and output a View (V), and both include a Number parameter (T/B). They are view manipulation components that read and potentially modify viewport state, with symmetric input/output signatures suggesting they act as view configurators.
Unit X and Unit Y are nearly identical: both take a single Number (F) and output a Vector (V). They are axis-aligned unit vector generators differing only in axis direction.
Unit X and Unit Z are nearly identical: both take a single Number (F) and output a Vector (V). They are axis-aligned unit vector generators differing only in axis direction.
Unit Y and Unit Z are nearly identical: both take a single Number (F) and output a Vector (V). They are axis-aligned unit vector generators differing only in axis direction.
Multiply and Divide are analogous operations: both take a Vector (V) and Number (F) and output a Vector (V) and Number (L). They perform inverse scalar operations on vectors.
Reverse and Unit Vector both take a single Vector (V) and output a single Vector (V). They are both unary vector transformation operations that produce a modified vector from input.

Cross Product and Dot Product share identical input signatures (Vector A, Vector B, Boolean U). Both are binary vector product operations with optional unitization flag, differing only in output type (Vector+Number vs Number).
Cross Product and Vector 2Pt share the Boolean (U) unitization flag and both output Vector (V) and Number (L). Both produce a vector with optional unitization and report the length.

Vector XYZ and Deconstruct Vector are inverse operations: Vector XYZ constructs a vector from X, Y, Z numbers, while Deconstruct Vector decomposes a vector into X, Y, Z numbers. They share the same three numeric components.
Multiply and Amplitude both take a Vector and a Number and output a Vector. Both scale a vector by a numeric factor, with Amplitude setting absolute length and Multiply scaling proportionally.
Vector Length and Vector XYZ both output a Number (L) representing vector length. Vector XYZ also outputs the vector itself, making them related in reporting vector magnitude.
Vector 2Pt and Dot Product both use a Boolean (U) input for unitization/normalization control, reflecting a shared pattern of optional unit normalization in vector operations.

Triangle Panels C and Triangle Panels B are nearly identical variants: same inputs (Srf, U, V) and same single Panels output. Both are triangular panel generators differing only in subdivision pattern.

Triangle Panels C and Triangular Panels A share identical I/O signatures (Srf, U, V → Panels) and both perform triangular surface panelization, differing only in the specific triangulation pattern (A vs C variant).
Triangle Panels B and Triangular Panels A share identical I/O signatures (Srf, U, V → Panels) and both perform triangular surface panelization, differing only in the specific triangulation variant.

Triangle Panels C and Staggered Quad Panels share identical I/O signatures (Srf, U, V → Panels). Both are surface panelization tools outputting panel geometry, differing in panel shape (triangle vs staggered quad).
Triangle Panels B and Staggered Quad Panels share identical I/O signatures (Srf, U, V → Panels). Both are surface panelization tools outputting a single Panels collection.
Triangular Panels A and Staggered Quad Panels share identical I/O signatures (Srf, U, V → Panels). Both subdivide a surface into panels with the same parameter structure.

Diamond Panels and Diamond Grid both operate on diamond/rhombus geometry patterns on surfaces with same (Srf, U, V) inputs. Both output multiple geometry collections related to diamond subdivision, making them closely related diamond-pattern tools.

Diamond Panels and Triangle Panels C share the same core inputs (Srf, U, V) and both output panel geometry collections. Diamond Panels also outputs Triangles, showing overlap with triangle panel components.
Diamond Panels and Triangle Panels B share the same core inputs (Srf, U, V). Diamond Panels outputs both Diamonds and Triangles, linking it to triangle panel variants.
Diamond Panels and Triangular Panels A share the same core inputs (Srf, U, V). Diamond Panels outputs Triangles as a secondary output, creating semantic overlap with triangular panel components.
Hexagon Cells and Diamond Panels both take (Srf, U, V) as core inputs and output multiple geometry collections (cells/panels + secondary geometry). Both are multi-output surface subdivision tools.

Hexagon Cells and Diamond Grid both take (Srf, U, V) as core inputs and produce multiple output collections including center/midpoint geometry. Both are grid-generation tools with richer output sets than simple panel tools.
Hexagon Cells and Triangle Panels C share the same core surface subdivision inputs (Srf, U, V). Both are LunchBox surface panelization components, with Hexagon Cells adding a thickness parameter t.
Diamond Grid and Triangle Panels C share the same core inputs (Srf, U, V) and belong to the same LunchBox panel family. Both subdivide surfaces into geometric cells, differing in output richness.

Triangular and Square share identical input signatures (P: Plane, S: Number, Ex: Integer, Ey: Integer) and identical output structure (C + P). Both are grid generation components producing cell curves/rectangles and center points.

Triangular and Hexagonal share identical input signatures (P: Plane, S: Number, Ex: Integer, Ey: Integer) and identical output types (C: Curve, P: Point). Both are polygon-based grid generators with the same parameter structure.
Square and Hexagonal share identical input signatures and both output a cell geometry plus Point. They differ only in output type (Rectangle vs Curve) but perform analogous grid tiling operations.

Rectangular and Square both output Rectangle + Point and share Plane input and Ex/Ey integer extent parameters. Both are rectangular grid generators; Rectangular adds separate Sx/Sy size params while Square uses a single S.
Rectangular and Triangular share Plane input, Ex/Ey extent integers, and Point output. Both are grid generators with the same extent control pattern, differing in cell shape and size parameter count.

Rectangular and Hexagonal share Plane input, Ex/Ey extent integers, and Point output. Both are grid generators controlling extent in two directions, differing only in cell geometry and output curve type.

Radial and Triangular both take a Plane and a Number size input, and both output Curve + Point. They are grid generators with similar I/O patterns though Radial uses radial/polar extent params (Er, Ep) instead of Cartesian (Ex, Ey).

Radial and Hexagonal both take Plane + Number inputs and output Curve + Point. Both are non-rectangular grid generators producing curved cell outlines, though their extent parameters differ (radial vs Cartesian).

Radial and Square share Plane + Number inputs and Point output. Both are grid generators in the same family, though Radial outputs Curve and uses polar extents while Square outputs Rectangle with Cartesian extents.

Braced Grid 2-D and Braced Grid 1-D are near-identical: same inputs (Srf, U, V) and same outputs (LinesA, LinesB, Nodes). They differ only in bracing direction (1D vs 2D), making them the closest pair in the set.

Braced Grid 2-D and Grid Structure share the same core inputs (Srf, U, V) and Nodes output. Both generate surface-based structural grids; the braced variant adds diagonal members (LinesB) on top of the base grid.

Braced Grid 1-D and Grid Structure share identical inputs (Srf, U, V) and Nodes output. Both are surface-based structural grid generators; the braced variant extends the base grid with additional diagonal lines.

Diagrid Structure and Grid Structure share the same output names (Lines, Nodes) and core inputs (Srf, U, V). Diagrid adds a Boolean toggle (T) for triangulation. Both produce line-based surface structures.

Diagrid Structure and Hexagonal Structure share identical output names (Lines, Nodes) and both have Srf, U, V, T inputs (Hexagonal also adds angle A). Both are surface-based structural pattern generators with a Boolean toggle.

Grid Structure and Hexagonal Structure share the same output signature (Lines, Nodes) and core inputs (Srf, U, V). Both generate surface-tessellation structural patterns; Hexagonal adds angle and Boolean parameters.

Braced Grid 2-D and Diagrid both take Surface + U/V integer grid divisions and output Nodes. They differ in output line structure (LinesA/LinesB vs Lines) but perform analogous surface-based structural grid generation.

Braced Grid 2-D and Space Truss Structure 2 share LinesA, LinesB, Nodes outputs and U/V integer inputs. Space Truss uses two surfaces (top/bottom chord) instead of one, extending the same structural grid concept into 3D.

Braced Grid 1-D and Space Truss Structure 2 share LinesA, LinesB, Nodes outputs and U/V grid inputs. Both generate multi-line structural members; Space Truss extends to dual-surface with additional Web output.

Space Truss Structure 2 and Grid Structure share U/V integer grid division inputs and Nodes output. Both are surface-based structural generators; Space Truss uses two surfaces for a 3D truss while Grid Structure uses one for a planar grid.

2D Truss and Space Truss Structure 2 both output LinesA, LinesB, and Nodes representing multi-chord structural systems. Both model truss-type structures with top/bottom chord lines and connecting members, though 2D Truss uses curves while Space Truss uses surfaces.
2D Truss and Braced Grid 2-D both output LinesA, LinesB, and Nodes. Both model braced structural systems with multiple line types; 2D Truss is curve-driven while Braced Grid is surface-driven.

Both components generate building masses on a plane with identical Width, Length, and floorHeight inputs, and produce the same Floors and Mass outputs. They differ only in how total building size is constrained: one uses a target Area (Number) while the other uses a floor count (Integer). They belong to the same lunchbox_mass family and are analogous operations for the same workflow, making them highly similar candidates for behavior and pattern propagation.

Both are Kangaroo2 'On' goal components that constrain points to a target geometry (Curve vs Mesh) with a Strength parameter. They share identical input structure (Points, target geometry, Strength) and identical output (P: Generic Data), differing only in the type of target geometry they constrain points onto.

Both are Wasp part-construction components that share a GEO input (geometry) and work with Generic Data types. Connection From Direction produces CONN output which is directly consumed as an input by Basic Part, making them tightly coupled in the same workflow stage.

Basic Part outputs PART and Get Part Geometry takes PART as input and outputs GEO — they are inverse/complementary operations on the same part object, sharing the PART Generic Data token and GEO geometry data.

Both Basic Part and Stochastic Aggregation operate on PART objects and RULES (aggregation rules), sharing the core Wasp assembly pipeline data tokens. Aggregation consumes parts produced by Basic Part.
Wasp Rule produces R (rule) output which feeds directly into RULES input of Stochastic Aggregation. Both are core Wasp aggregation-logic components operating on connection and part relationship data.

Connection From Direction defines connections (CONN) between parts, and Rule references those connections (C1, C2) to define assembly rules. Both deal with the connection topology layer of the Wasp system.
Both are collision/physics components that take a Strength (Number) parameter and output Generic Data (collision results). Both simulate physical interactions between geometric entities.

Both are sphere/object collision components sharing Strength (Number) and radius/radii (Number) inputs with Generic Data output. SphereCollide uses Points+R while Collider uses Objects+Radii — analogous sphere-based collision patterns.
Both are UI/interactive widget components with no formal inputs or outputs — they are standalone interactive controls (Digit Scroller and Colour Picker) embedded in the canvas.
Both are UI widget/display components with no formal inputs or outputs, serving as interactive or display elements on the canvas.
Both are UI display/interactive components with no formal inputs or outputs.

Both are colour-related UI components with no formal inputs or outputs. Colour Picker selects colours interactively; Object Display Colour sets display colour — both deal with colour assignment in the Rhino/GH environment.

boolean_input.name: boolean_input
boolean_input.typical_gotcha: Boolean trigger inputs (like Write) are edge-sensitive in some components; toggling false-to-true is required to fire action

domain2_input.name: domain2_input
domain2_input.typical_gotcha: Domain² requires a valid 2D domain; ensure both U and V ranges are non-zero to avoid degenerate subdivision

vector_output.name: vector_output
vector_output.typical_gotcha: Vectors from Deconstruct Plane are unit axes; vectors from moment calculations are not normalized

annotation_style_io.name: annotation_style_io
annotation_style_io.typical_gotcha: Annotation styles must exist in the Rhino document; referencing a non-existent style causes null output

number_param_output.name: number_param_output
number_param_output.typical_gotcha: Number outputs representing parameters (t values) are normalized 0-1 only on reparameterized curves; raw domain values otherwise

t_param_curve.name: t_param_curve
t_param_curve.typical_gotcha: t parameter is in curve domain units, not normalized 0-1; use Reparameterize or Evaluate Curve with domain remapping if needed

surface_input.name: surface_input
surface_input.typical_gotcha: Surface must be valid and not degenerate; trim boundaries are not accounted for in raw surface evaluation

surface_output.name: surface_output
surface_output.typical_gotcha: Cylinder output is an open surface; cap it with Brep operations if a closed solid is needed

integer_degree_param.name: integer_degree_param
integer_degree_param.typical_gotcha: Degree must be between 1 and 11 in Grasshopper; degree higher than point count minus 1 will cause errors

boolean_toggle_input.name: boolean_toggle_input
boolean_toggle_input.typical_gotcha: Boolean inputs often control tangency or reset behavior; toggling mid-stream may cause unexpected recomputation

vector_input.name: vector_input
vector_input.typical_gotcha: Vectors are not automatically unitized; unnormalized vectors may produce unexpected scaling in direction-based operations

number_length_param.name: number_length_param
number_length_param.typical_gotcha: Length parameter must be positive; zero length produces degenerate geometry

domain_input.name: domain_input
domain_input.typical_gotcha: Domain must have min < max; inverted domains may cause unexpected behavior in clamping or rectangle sizing

number_output.name: number_output
number_output.typical_gotcha: Number outputs like length or parameter values are context-dependent; check units and domain before using downstream

enum_type_input.name: enum_type_input
enum_type_input.typical_gotcha: Enum-style inputs require values within valid range (typically 0-2); out-of-range causes component error

wrap_index_input.name: wrap_index_input
wrap_index_input.typical_gotcha: W=false causes null when index is out of list bounds; W=true wraps index cyclically

list_index_input.name: list_index_input
list_index_input.typical_gotcha: Negative indices not supported unless wrap is enabled; 0-based indexing

format_string_input.name: format_string_input
format_string_input.typical_gotcha: Placeholder count in format string must match number of data inputs (0, 1, ...)

sweep_rail_input.name: sweep_rail_input
sweep_rail_input.typical_gotcha: Rails must not intersect each other; profile curve must intersect both rails for valid sweep

loft_section_input.name: loft_section_input
loft_section_input.typical_gotcha: Section curves must be compatible degree/point-count for fit loft; mismatched curves cause poor fit

circle_input.name: circle_input
circle_input.typical_gotcha: Circle inputs expect valid non-zero radius; degenerate circles cause transformation or annotation failures

text_pattern_input.name: text_pattern_input
text_pattern_input.typical_gotcha: Text pattern inputs use wildcard or regex matching; an empty pattern may return all or no items depending on implementation

model_material_io.name: model_material_io
model_material_io.typical_gotcha: Model Material components act as pass-through editors; changes affect the Rhino document material directly

number_deviation_output.name: number_deviation_output
number_deviation_output.typical_gotcha: Deviation output (dx) represents RMS fit error; large values indicate points do not lie on a plane

mesh_face_output.name: mesh_face_output
mesh_face_output.typical_gotcha: Mesh face indices must reference valid vertex indices; out-of-range indices cause invalid mesh construction

complex_output.name: complex_output
complex_output.typical_gotcha: Complex number outputs require Grasshopper complex-aware components downstream; cannot wire directly to standard number inputs

number_param_input.name: number_param_input
number_param_input.typical_gotcha: Number inputs may need domain clamping; negative values can cause errors in geometric operations

integer_param_input.name: integer_param_input
integer_param_input.typical_gotcha: Integer indices are zero-based; out-of-range values cause null outputs

matrix_passthrough.name: matrix_passthrough
matrix_passthrough.typical_gotcha: Column indices are zero-based; swapping identical indices has no effect

distance_number.name: distance_number
distance_number.typical_gotcha: D param is reused for distance, depth, and contour spacing — ensure correct unit scale; very small or zero values cause degenerate geometry

enum_type.name: enum_type
enum_type.typical_gotcha: Enum inputs require integer index (0, 1, 2) or matched string; passing arbitrary integers outside valid range causes errors

naked_edge_enum.name: naked_edge_enum
naked_edge_enum.typical_gotcha: Controls how naked (boundary) edges are handled during subdivision; default (0) keeps edges fixed

vector_normal.name: vector_normal
vector_normal.typical_gotcha: N/D vector must be non-zero; zero-length vectors cause contour or array operations to produce no output

axis_line.name: axis_line
axis_line.typical_gotcha: Revolution axis line must pass through or near the profile curve; misaligned axis produces self-intersecting or invalid Brep

revolution_profile.name: revolution_profile
revolution_profile.typical_gotcha: Profile curve (P) for revolution should be planar and on the same plane as the axis for predictable results

sum_surface_curves.name: sum_surface_curves
sum_surface_curves.typical_gotcha: Sum Surface requires two curves with compatible parameterization; mismatched domain lengths cause twisted or degenerate surfaces

zombie_solver_goals.name: zombie_solver_goals
zombie_solver_goals.typical_gotcha: GoalObjects must be Kangaroo goal objects; passing raw geometry will cause solver to fail silently

loft_options_output.name: loft_options_output
loft_options_output.typical_gotcha: Loft Options output must be connected to a Loft component's options input; T integer controls loft type (0=Normal,1=Loose,2=Tight,3=Straight,4=Developable,5=Uniform)

file_write_pattern.name: file_write_pattern
file_write_pattern.typical_gotcha: Write trigger should be a Button not a Toggle to avoid continuous file writing on every solution

transform_input.name: transform_input
transform_input.typical_gotcha: Transform matrices must be valid; identity or zero transforms produce no change or collapse geometry

box_output.name: box_output
box_output.typical_gotcha: Box orientation depends on input plane; world-aligned vs oriented boxes differ for containment and boolean ops

generic_data_math.name: generic_data_math
generic_data_math.typical_gotcha: Math operations on Generic Data rely on implicit casting; non-numeric inputs will cause runtime errors

subd_io.name: subd_io
subd_io.typical_gotcha: SubD geometry requires Rhino 7+; passing standard Brep or Mesh will cause type mismatch errors

model_environment_io.name: model_environment_io
model_environment_io.typical_gotcha: Model Environment parameters are renderer-specific; not all rendering engines support all environment types

nurbs_curve_degree.name: nurbs_curve_degree
nurbs_curve_degree.typical_gotcha: NURBS degree must be between 1 and 11; degree higher than point count minus 1 causes construction failure

box_input.name: box_input
box_input.typical_gotcha: Box must have non-zero dimensions in all axes; degenerate boxes produce invalid mesh output

domain_output.name: domain_output
domain_output.typical_gotcha: Curve domain output reflects the raw curve parameterization which may not be 0-1 normalized

list_manipulation_output.name: list_manipulation_output
list_manipulation_output.typical_gotcha: List operations output data trees that may need flattening or grafting depending on input tree structure

time_input.name: time_input
time_input.typical_gotcha: Time inputs require DateTime formatted data; plain numbers will not be accepted without conversion

time_output.name: time_output
time_output.typical_gotcha: Date Range output count is N+1 points spanning A to B; ensure N matches expected interval count

integer_enum_input.name: integer_enum_input
integer_enum_input.typical_gotcha: Enum-style integers typically valid in range 0-2; out-of-range values may silently clamp or error

generic_data_io.name: generic_data_io
generic_data_io.typical_gotcha: Generic Data bypasses type checking; downstream components may fail if actual type is incompatible

uv_division_params.name: uv_division_params
uv_division_params.typical_gotcha: U and V count parameters control grid density; high values significantly increase computation time

math_function_xy.name: math_function_xy
math_function_xy.typical_gotcha: Math function components operate element-wise on lists; input x should be numeric, output y is the transformed value

solver_goals_input.name: solver_goals_input
solver_goals_input.typical_gotcha: Goals must be properly constructed goal objects; mixing incompatible goal types causes solver instability

matrix_io.name: matrix_io
matrix_io.typical_gotcha: Matrix dimensions must be compatible with downstream operations; transposing a non-square matrix changes row/column counts

enum_input.name: enum_input
enum_input.typical_gotcha: Enum parameters accept integer indices (0-based); passing out-of-range integers causes silent fallback to default

boolean_io.name: boolean_io
boolean_io.typical_gotcha: Boolean inputs labeled 'H' (hidden) toggle visibility; ensure correct True/False semantics per component

uv_subdivision_inputs.name: uv_subdivision_inputs
uv_subdivision_inputs.typical_gotcha: U and V subdivision counts should be balanced; very high values cause performance issues without quality gain

model_content_io.name: model_content_io
model_content_io.typical_gotcha: Model Content is a Rhino.Inside/Revit-specific type; not available in standalone Grasshopper

uv_count_params.name: uv_count_params
uv_count_params.typical_gotcha: U and V subdivision counts must be >= 1; very high values cause performance issues; surface domain must be valid before meshing

weight_output.name: weight_output
weight_output.typical_gotcha: Control point weights are 1.0 for non-rational curves/surfaces; modifying weights changes the NURBS shape non-intuitively

perp_frame_output.name: perp_frame_output
perp_frame_output.typical_gotcha: Perp Frame at t parameter may flip orientation along the curve; use Aligned Perp Frames for consistent orientation across multiple frames

number_factor_input.name: number_factor_input
number_factor_input.typical_gotcha: Default value of 0 or 1 may produce degenerate geometry; always supply explicit values

uv_division_input.name: uv_division_input
uv_division_input.typical_gotcha: U/V count must be >= 1; very high values cause performance issues

sort_key_input.name: sort_key_input
sort_key_input.typical_gotcha: Key list length must match data list length; mismatched lengths cause partial sorting or errors

area_centroid_output.name: area_centroid_output
area_centroid_output.typical_gotcha: Centroid is computed in world space; for non-planar geometry, result may not lie on the surface

matrix_input.name: matrix_input
matrix_input.typical_gotcha: Row indices are 0-based; swapping out-of-range rows causes errors

matrix_output.name: matrix_output
matrix_output.typical_gotcha: Matrix dimensions are preserved; only row order changes after swap

subd_input.name: subd_input
subd_input.typical_gotcha: SubD must be converted from mesh or NURBS before use; not all Rhino geometry converts cleanly to SubD topology

generic_constraint_output.name: generic_constraint_output
generic_constraint_output.typical_gotcha: Constraint outputs must be collected into a list and passed to a solver component; they are not directly displayable geometry

n_count_input.name: n_count_input
n_count_input.typical_gotcha: Frame count N determines subdivision density along curve; very high values slow computation with minimal visual gain

comparison_number_input.name: comparison_number_input
comparison_number_input.typical_gotcha: A and B must be comparable numeric types; mixing integers and floats may cause unexpected precision issues

render_attributes_passthrough.name: render_attributes_passthrough
render_attributes_passthrough.typical_gotcha: Render Attributes components act as pass-through editors; modifying one property does not reset others unless explicitly overridden

number_scale_param.name: number_scale_param
number_scale_param.typical_gotcha: Scale/size values must be positive; very large or very small values can cause performance issues

geometry_passthrough.name: geometry_passthrough
geometry_passthrough.typical_gotcha: Generic geometry input accepts many types but downstream components may require specific types; casting errors common

boolean_flag_input.name: boolean_flag_input
boolean_flag_input.typical_gotcha: Default true/false behavior varies per component; always check component documentation for meaning of each flag

integer_count_input.name: integer_count_input
integer_count_input.typical_gotcha: Very high counts cause performance issues; minimum values (e.g. 3 for polygon sides) must be respected

field_output.name: field_output
field_output.typical_gotcha: Fields must be evaluated at points; direct visualization requires a field display or evaluation component

annotation_style_passthrough.name: annotation_style_passthrough
annotation_style_passthrough.typical_gotcha: Annotation styles must exist in the Rhino document; missing styles cause null output

box_bounds_input.name: box_bounds_input
box_bounds_input.typical_gotcha: Box defines the region of influence; degenerate boxes (zero volume) cause undefined behavior

integer_uv_grid.name: integer_uv_grid
integer_uv_grid.typical_gotcha: U/V count values below 1 cause errors; high values dramatically increase geometry count

integer_degree_input.name: integer_degree_input
integer_degree_input.typical_gotcha: Degree must be >= 1 and <= N-1 for valid knot vectors; mismatched values cause null output

number_strength_input.name: number_strength_input
number_strength_input.typical_gotcha: Strength values near 0 may cause solver instability; very high values can cause simulation divergence

number_scale_angle_input.name: number_scale_angle_input
number_scale_angle_input.typical_gotcha: Angle inputs may expect radians or degrees depending on component; check units carefully

transform_io.name: transform_io
transform_io.typical_gotcha: Inverse of a singular or near-singular transform may produce unstable results

integer_count_output.name: integer_count_output
integer_count_output.typical_gotcha: Count outputs reflect list lengths which may vary per branch in a data tree

subd_output.name: subd_output
subd_output.typical_gotcha: MultiPipe SubD output may have non-manifold topology if input curves share endpoints incorrectly

mesh_parameters_output.name: mesh_parameters_output
mesh_parameters_output.typical_gotcha: Speed settings prioritize fast meshing over quality; may produce coarse meshes unsuitable for rendering

rectangle_input.name: rectangle_input
rectangle_input.typical_gotcha: Rectangle must be planar; 3D bounding rectangles are not supported by all components

path_output.name: path_output
path_output.typical_gotcha: Path outputs reflect the data tree structure; flat lists have a single {0} path

view_output.name: view_output
view_output.typical_gotcha: View output must be connected to Make2D or similar components; not directly renderable

passthrough_settings_io.name: passthrough_settings_io
passthrough_settings_io.typical_gotcha: Settings components pass through all parameters unchanged unless explicitly modified; useful as inspection nodes but easy to overlook that values are passthrough

number_factor.name: number_factor
number_factor.typical_gotcha: Number inputs often expect values in specific ranges (e.g., 0-1 for factors, positive for radii); no automatic clamping

number_output_channel.name: number_output_channel
number_output_channel.typical_gotcha: Number outputs from split or decompose operations are typically normalized (0-1) or in radians; verify units before arithmetic

angle_param.name: angle_param
angle_param.typical_gotcha: Angle is in radians by default in Grasshopper; use DegToRad conversion if supplying degrees

boolean_logic_input.name: boolean_logic_input
boolean_logic_input.typical_gotcha: Both A and B inputs must be provided; missing input defaults to false which affects XOR result

wasp_generic_data.name: wasp_generic_data
wasp_generic_data.typical_gotcha: Wasp components use opaque Generic Data types; outputs must be connected to matching Wasp input slots and cannot be inspected directly without Wasp-specific components

list_input.name: list_input
list_input.typical_gotcha: Sub List requires a valid Domain within list index bounds; out-of-range domains cause empty output

predicate_input.typical_gotcha: Predicate type is specific to filter components; standard Boolean cannot be directly substituted

predicate_output.name: predicate_output
predicate_output.typical_gotcha: Logical Or Filter output predicate must be consumed by a compatible filter component, not a standard Boolean gate

xyz_coordinate_output.name: xyz_coordinate_output
xyz_coordinate_output.typical_gotcha: Coordinates are relative to the input plane S, not world XY; ensure correct reference plane is connected
